topLine: GPT-5.6 Pro finds a counterexample to the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans cost conjecture.

items.headline: GPT-5.6 Pro finds a counterexample to the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans cost conjecture
items.summary: Dmitry Rybin reported that GPT-5.6 Pro produced a small directed graph where the fractional flow costs 58, but every unsplittable flow within the allowed congestion costs at least 60. This refutes a roughly 30-year-old conjecture in combinatorial optimization that unsplittable flows can match the fractional cost; the 1999 congestion-only theorem is unaffected. Rybin published the chat transcript. Several people have checked the arithmetic informally, but no named expert verification or peer-reviewed paper has appeared.
